## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the latency numbers and the cache line argument from memory.
- Say honestly what you can and cannot do in C++, in the words you would use in an interview.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>35 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Finish anything outstanding from days 316 to 321. The C++ book verified against the Python one is the artifact worth having, because it is the concrete thing behind any claim you make.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Closed book: the latency card, the cache line argument, the container crossover, and the four-way decomposition of your speedup. Then write the two sentences you would actually say when asked about C++.

## Drill <span class='task-total'>interview thread</span>

Spaced repetition, not cramming. Every drill in the year is collected on the [drills page](../drills.qmd).

::: {.task-list .drill}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Timed mixed set, seventh sitting: five problems in fifteen minutes. Score and plot.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> A systems question: you need to store five years of tick data for 500 symbols and query arbitrary time ranges. Describe your storage design in two minutes, out loud, with the latency numbers behind each choice. This is a question with no single right answer and the reasoning is what is scored.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Market making, fourth sitting: I quote a market in a quantity you can estimate better than I can. Trade with me, then tell me what you learned from the fact that I was willing to trade at that price.
:::
:::
